_comment: Read by .github/scripts/protected-paths.mjs on every pull request. Two shapes:
'protected_tests' are exact file paths -- a change matches only that file, never a
same-named file elsewhere or a longer name that merely starts with it (blocking.test.ts.bak
is not blocking.test.ts). 'protected_paths' are exact paths or globs ('**' crosses directory
boundaries, '*' does not) -- anything under them is protected, source and tests alike.
The four tests judge the reviewer: its blocking, remediation and decision-order tests, and
the runner's security test. The sample fixtures are
what the reviewer is scored on -- a fixture is never weakened because the reviewer missed it,
so a pull request may not answer a miss by editing the fixture that caught it.
The reviewer's own prompt and code are deliberately NOT protected. A change to the reviewer is
the contribution this repository invites; what holds it honest is its regression score, quoted
in the pull request, not a refusal to let it be written. A rule that protected the prompt would
refuse the very pull request CONTRIBUTING.md asks for.
The only path that may change these: a maintainer's release commit on the default branch,
which this check does not run against -- see CONTRIBUTING.md.
